studies.label: Supervised college-student mathematical creativity experiment

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 43), Figure 1, printed arm labels; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 45), Participants; withdrawals described on PDF p. 4 (printed p. 42), Procedure

arms.name: Experimental (task resolution with ChatGPT)
arms.description: Students used ChatGPT on personal computers with introductory training and structured example, heuristic, task-reminder, critical-thinking and divergent-thinking prompts. They could iteratively request and refine solutions. PDF pp. 5-7 (printed pp. 43-45), Procedure, Figures 1-2 and Table 1.

arms.name: Control (task resolution without ChatGPT)
arms.description: Students solved the same tasks using traditional tools such as paper and pencil, without support or external prompts. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 43), Figure 1 and Procedure.

studies.task: Produce multiple solutions to four open-ended mathematics tasks involving grid figures, dispersion of marbles, water in a tilted rectangular prism, and common properties of geometric shapes (PDF p. 8, printed p. 46, MCT; PDF p. 9, printed p. 47, Figure 3).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (GPT-4o)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 6 (printed p. 44), Figure 2, visible model label "ChatGPT 4o"; PDF p. 2 (printed p. 40), ChatGPT, names GPT-4o but does not establish its release year.

studies.shared_sample: Possible, unconfirmed overlap with c089: Liu et al. (2025), Who Is the Best Helper for University Students' Mathematical Creativity? (DOI 10.1002/cae.70100). Its Human-ChatGPT group and c471's Experimental group have the same analyzed size and identical reported age mean/SD, gender, major and prior ChatGPT experience counts. This cross-paper match suggests possible overlap but does not establish shared participants. Neither examined recruitment account identifies a shared sample; author confirmation is needed for shared-sample handling in pooled estimates.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Number of distinct correct-answer categories within a participant’s solutions. Two scorers independently classified correct solutions and resolved disagreements; each participant’s indicator was summed across the four tasks. Scorer qualifications and blinding are not reported (PDF pp. 9-10, printed pp. 47-48, Mathematical creativity scoring).

open_items: Initial randomized totals and withdrawals by arm are not reported. Figure 1 and the Participants section provide retained-sample counts, not a separate allocation/attrition account (PDF pp. 4-5 and 7, printed pp. 42-43 and 45).

The title/abstract calls the study quasi-experimental, but Methods explicitly states that all students were randomly assigned. Sequence generation and allocation concealment are not described (PDF pp. 1 and 4, printed pp. 39 and 42).
The originality frequency reference pool and exact category-frequency boundary conventions are not defined; scorer qualifications and blinding are not stated (PDF pp. 9-10, printed pp. 47-48).
The standardizing denominator for Table 5 d values is not specified. Participant-level arm means and SDs are printed, so no denominator has been inferred (PDF p. 11, printed p. 49).
Adjusted ANCOVA arm means, adjusted differences, standard errors and confidence intervals are not reported (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 49-50).

The exact GPT-4o snapshot and release year are not established by the paper. The literature review cites OpenAI (2023) alongside GPT-4o, which is a citation year rather than an explicit release-year statement. ai_tool.year is null (PDF pp. 2 and 6, printed pp. 40 and 44).

The reconciled screening form flags possible shared participants with c089. This paper does not explicitly confirm shared participants; preserve the uncertainty for shared-sample handling. The cross-paper overlap flag is carried forward from forms/c471.json, sample_overlap.
notes: Extraction B. The complete markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks through the final citation, and PDF tables and figures were examined directly with pymupdf. No appendix or supplementary section is present or listed in the retrieval entry. Eligible-statistic inventory: Table 5 reports arm means and SDs, t statistics and degrees of freedom, d and p for flexibility, fluency and originality; the Results text reports adjusted F statistics and degrees of freedom, partial eta squared and p for each of the same outcomes. These are six analysis records for three outcomes in one sample. There is no reported post-intervention overall-creativity composite, across-person diversity measure or output produced after AI removal. This is an individually randomized supervised experiment under the explicit Methods statement: "All students were randomly assigned to either the experimental group (task resolution with ChatGPT) or the control group (task resolution without ChatGPT)." Both conditions were represented during classroom sessions (PDF p. 4, printed p. 42); sessions are not the assignment unit. The intervention combines ChatGPT with structured prompting support. Arm sizes are explicit text labels embedded in the Figure 1 image, visually verified by rendering PDF p. 5; a checker using only PDF text extraction may flag their quotes. No chart positions were digitized, and no effect, SD, SE, interval, count or p-value was derived. Quotes retain printed numerical precision. Extraction date: 2026-10-11.
